questions.stem: The marketing team ___ the final report before the board meeting started.

fr.rule: Le plus-que-parfait (had + participe passé) exprime une action terminée avant une autre action passée (ici « started »).
why_wrong: A : le présent simple ne convient pas à une action passée.
C : le futur est incompatible avec « started ».
D : le present perfect ne se combine pas avec un repère passé précis.
fr.example: She had left the office before the call began.

en.rule: The past perfect (had + past participle) shows an action completed before another past action (here 'started').
why_wrong: A: the simple present does not fit a past action.
C: the future contradicts 'started'.
D: the present perfect cannot be used with a finished past time reference.
en.example: She had left the office before the call began.

questions.stem: Each of the new employees ___ required to attend the safety training.

fr.rule: « Each (of) » est suivi d'un verbe au singulier, même devant un nom pluriel.
why_wrong: A : « were » est pluriel et au passé.
B : « have been » est pluriel.
D : « are » est pluriel.
fr.example: Each of the managers has a private office.

en.rule: 'Each (of)' takes a singular verb, even before a plural noun.
why_wrong: A: 'were' is plural and past.
B: 'have been' is plural.
D: 'are' is plural.
en.example: Each of the managers has a private office.

questions.stem: All invoices must ___ to the accounting department by the end of the month.

fr.rule: Après un modal (must), on utilise l'infinitif sans « to ». Le sujet « invoices » subit l'action : voix passive, donc « be + participe passé ».
why_wrong: B : le gérondif ne suit pas un modal.
C : forme active, mais les factures ne se soumettent pas elles-mêmes.
D : « have submitted » est actif et demande un complément d'objet.
fr.example: The documents must be signed before Friday.

en.rule: After a modal (must) use the bare infinitive. The subject 'invoices' receives the action, so the passive 'be + past participle' is needed.
why_wrong: B: a gerund cannot follow a modal.
C: active form, but invoices do not submit themselves.
D: 'have submitted' is active and needs an object.
en.example: The documents must be signed before Friday.

questions.stem: The conference will take place ___ Tuesday, March 14, at the Grand Hotel.

fr.rule: On utilise « on » devant un jour ou une date précise.
why_wrong: A : « by » signifie « avant / au plus tard ».
B : « at » s'emploie pour les heures et lieux précis.
C : « in » s'emploie pour les mois, années, saisons.

en.rule: Use 'on' before a specific day or date.
why_wrong: A: 'by' means 'no later than'.
B: 'at' is for clock times and precise places.
C: 'in' is for months, years and seasons.

questions.stem: ___ the sales figures were lower than expected, the company decided to expand into new markets.

fr.rule: « Although » introduit une proposition complète (sujet + verbe) exprimant une opposition.
why_wrong: A : « because of » est suivi d'un nom, et exprime la cause.
C : « therefore » est un adverbe de conséquence, il ne relie pas deux propositions seul.
D : « despite » est suivi d'un nom ou d'un gérondif, pas d'une proposition.
fr.example: Although it rained, the event went ahead.

en.rule: 'Although' introduces a full clause (subject + verb) showing contrast.
why_wrong: A: 'because of' is followed by a noun and expresses cause.
C: 'therefore' is a conjunctive adverb of result and cannot join two clauses on its own.
D: 'despite' takes a noun or gerund, not a clause.
en.example: Although it rained, the event went ahead.

questions.stem: Ms. Tanaka, ___ has managed our Osaka branch for ten years, will join the head office next month.

fr.rule: « who » est sujet du verbe « has managed » et remplace une personne.
why_wrong: A : « whose » exprime la possession et serait suivi d'un nom.
C : « whom » est complément, mais ici le pronom est sujet.
D : « which » remplace une chose.
fr.example: The clerk who helped me was very kind.

en.rule: 'who' is the subject of 'has managed' and refers to a person.
why_wrong: A: 'whose' shows possession and would be followed by a noun.
C: 'whom' is an object pronoun, but here the pronoun is the subject.
D: 'which' refers to things.
en.example: The clerk who helped me was very kind.

questions.stem: The company's ___ to customer satisfaction has earned it several industry awards.

fr.rule: Après « The company's », un nom est attendu (sujet de « has earned »). « commitment » est le nom.
why_wrong: A : le gérondif « committing » est un verbe, pas le nom attendu après un possessif.
B : participe/adjectif, pas un nom.
D : verbe.
fr.example: Her commitment to quality impressed the clients.

en.rule: After 'The company's' a noun is needed (subject of 'has earned'). 'commitment' is the noun.
why_wrong: A: the gerund 'committing' is verb-like, not the noun expected after a possessive.
B: participle/adjective, not a noun.
D: verb.
en.example: Her commitment to quality impressed the clients.

questions.stem: If the shipment ___ on time, we would have met the client's deadline.

fr.rule: Condition irréelle dans le passé : If + plus-que-parfait, … would have + participe passé.
why_wrong: A : le present perfect ne convient pas à une condition passée irréelle.
B : le présent mène à un conditionnel de type 1.
C : « would » ne s'emploie pas dans la proposition en « if ».
fr.example: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train.

en.rule: Third conditional: If + past perfect, … would have + past participle.
why_wrong: A: the present perfect does not fit an unreal past condition.
B: the present gives a first conditional.
C: 'would' is not used in the 'if' clause.
en.example: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train.

questions.stem: Our new software is ___ than the previous version, so tasks are completed in half the time.

fr.rule: « than » appelle un comparatif. Pour un adjectif long : more + adjectif.
why_wrong: A : forme de base, sans comparaison.
B : « the » est déplacé après « is … than ».
D : superlatif, incompatible avec « than ».
fr.example: This route is more direct than the highway.

en.rule: 'than' requires a comparative. For long adjectives use more + adjective.
why_wrong: A: base form, no comparison.
B: 'the' does not belong in 'is … than'.
D: superlative, which cannot take 'than'.
en.example: This route is more direct than the highway.

questions.stem: The director suggested ___ the launch of the product until the following quarter.

fr.rule: Le verbe « suggest » est suivi d'un gérondif (-ing), jamais de « to + infinitif ».
why_wrong: A : la forme de base ne suit pas « suggested » ici.
B : « to » + gérondif n'a pas de sens dans cette structure.
D : « suggest to do » est incorrect.

en.rule: The verb 'suggest' is followed by a gerund (-ing), never 'to + infinitive'.
why_wrong: A: the base form does not follow 'suggested' here.
B: 'to' + gerund makes no sense in this structure.
D: 'suggest to do' is incorrect.
